newsitem.title: GERMANY: High cobalt prices cause consumer concern-Erasteel.
newsitem.headline: High cobalt prices cause consumer concern-Erasteel.

text.p: High cobalt prices are causing consumer concern, Jacques Bacardats, chief executive officer at speed steel producer Erasteel, said on Wednesday.
But Bacardats, who was talking to Reuters during a nickel industry meeting organised by Erasteel's holding group Eramet, expected a price reversal in the third quarter.

He said the price increases were due to civil war in Zaire and the suspension of U.S. stockpile cobalt sales due to a legal dispute between the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) and Minor Metals Inc.
"The two factors have been enough to tip the balance after steady conditions in early 1997," Badardats said.
"The price could increase further in the coming weeks but we hope it will return to normal after that."
He endorsed a Reuters price report of $24.10 cents/lb cif Rotterdam for Zambian cobalt, basis April 29.
Traders believe the price of the minor metal, which is used in Erasteel's products for the tool industry, could go to $27 or $30 before the Zairean crisis is resolved.
Prices were around $22 at the end of January.
Bacardats said Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila should quickly restart mines after seizing power and the DLA problems should be resolved.
He added prices of molybdenum, another raw material, were neutral and those of vanadium too high, but the effects were being passed on to, and absorbed by, Erasteel's customers.
Erasteel has a 30 percent share in the world speed steel market if China and the former USSR are excluded.
Sales of the steel fell by 11 or 12 percent globally last year and Erasteel's dropped 13 percent to 25,228 tonnes.
Lower sales are again forecast for first half 1997 but prices should hold stable, Erasteel said.
The company is exploring new areas of usage.
